title: Artificial Intelligence
weightage: ~6–10 marks (roughly 3–6 questions) per GATE DA paper (2024–2026)
summary: Highly scorable, algorithm-tracing section: expect BFS/DFS/UCS/A* node-expansion order and heuristic admissibility/consistency, minimax values and alpha-beta pruned nodes, propositional/first-order logic validity and translations, and Bayesian-network questions on conditional independence, variable elimination and sampling.
notesGuide: 1) Use the free Berkeley CS188 online textbook (inst.eecs.berkeley.edu/~cs188/textbook) as the main notes - read Search (state spaces, uninformed, informed), Games (minimax), Logic (propositional, FOL, inference) and Bayes Nets (representation, d-separation, elimination, approximate) sections; these map exactly to the syllabus. 2) Keep AIMA's free pseudocode PDF (aima.cs.berkeley.edu/algorithms.pdf) for exact algorithm definitions (graph vs tree search, alpha-beta, resolution, enumeration, rejection/likelihood weighting). 3) Watch MIT 6.034 Lectures 4-6 (search & games) and 21-22 (probabilistic inference) and the NPTEL Mausam course for depth. 4) Make short notes as tables: for each search algorithm -> fringe data structure, complete?, optimal?, time/space, tie-breaking convention; for heuristics -> admissible/consistent definitions + dominance; for games -> alpha/beta update rules and pruning condition with one fully worked tree. 5) For logic, keep a 1-page sheet of equivalences (De Morgan, implication, contrapositive), CNF conversion, resolution, quantifier negation and common English->FOL patterns; reuse your Discrete Maths logic notes. 6) For Bayes nets, write the factorization rule, the three d-separation triples (causal chain, common cause, common effect) and a worked variable-elimination example, plus prior/rejection/likelihood-weighting/Gibbs sampling steps. 7) Practise with CS188 Fall 2024 exam-prep worksheets (with solutions), then GATE DA PYQs and the old GATE CSE AI questions on GATE Overflow.
